# 1 Clement Chapter 1 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 1 Clement 1 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/1CL_001_page_001.jpg

---

## Salutation

**1:Salutation** The church of God sojourning in Rome to the church of God sojourning in Corinth, to those called and sanctified by the will of God through our Lord Jesus Christ: grace and peace be multiplied to you from God Almighty, through Jesus Christ.

---

## Chapter 1

**1:1** Because of the sudden and repeated calamities and misfortunes which have befallen us, brothers, we consider that we have been somewhat slow in turning our attention to the matters disputed among you, beloved, and to the detestable and unholy schism, so alien and foreign to the chosen of God, which a few rash and headstrong persons have kindled to such a pitch of madness that your venerable and celebrated name, worthy of all love, has been greatly slandered.

**1:2** For who that had sojourned among you did not prove your most virtuous and steadfast faith? Who did not marvel at your sober and temperate piety in Christ? Who did not proclaim the magnificent character of your hospitality? Who did not pronounce blessed your perfect and sound knowledge?

**1:3** For you did all things without partiality, and you walked in the laws of God, submissive to your rulers and paying all fitting honor to the older among you. The young you enjoined to hold temperate and seemly thoughts. The women you charged to fulfill all things in a blameless and seemly and pure conscience, rendering due affection to their husbands; and you taught them to remain in the rule of obedience and to manage their households with dignity and all discretion.

---

*EMET renders the Greek of Codex Alexandrinus with maximal literalness. Salutation reconstructed from manuscript evidence.*
